findings.title: getClientsWithPermission only matches the 'all-clients' meta-resource, not individual client resources
findings.body: getClientsWithPermission() calls resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...) to find resources of type 'Clients'. However, the per-client resources created in AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource() (resourceStore.create(resourceServer, name, resourceServer.getClientId())) never call resource.setType(...); only the single meta resource representing the whole resource type ('Clients') gets its type set during AdminPermissionsSchema.init(). As a result, findByType will only ever return that one meta resource, so getClientsWithPermission() cannot discover individual per-client grants and would at best add the literal resource name 'Clients' (not an actual client id) to the result set when an 'all clients' permission is granted. Any caller relying on this method to filter/list clients a caller has permission for (e.g. client listing endpoints) will silently miss clients granted via individual resource permissions.

findings.title: getResourceName() was not updated to handle the new CLIENTS resource type
findings.body: getResourceName() has special-case handling that maps a 'Users' resource to a friendly display ('All users' for the all-resource meta entry, or the username for a specific user resource). No equivalent branch was added for the new CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE/CLIENTS resource type introduced by this PR. For permissions scoped to 'Clients' it falls through to resource.getDisplayName(), which is never set when the resource is created in getOrCreateResource() (displayName isn't populated there), and there's no 'All clients' label for the all-resource meta entry either. This results in blank/unclear resource names being shown for Client-type permissions (e.g. in the admin console or REST responses), unlike the equivalent User-type permissions.

findings.title: Potential NullPointerException when the 'all-clients' meta resource is missing
findings.body: In hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope), when the per-client resource is null, the code falls back to AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(session, server, CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) to get the 'all-clients' resource, then immediately calls authz.getStoreFactory().getPolicyStore().findByResource(server, resource) without checking whether that call returned null. getResourceTypeResource() returns null if the resourceType is unknown or if resourceStore.findByName() doesn't find the meta resource (e.g. the admin-permissions client's resource server hasn't been fully initialized). In that case findByResource is invoked with a null resource, which is likely to throw a NullPointerException instead of gracefully denying the permission.

findings.title: Role/Client/Group removal cleanup gated only by legacy (V1) feature flag, not V2
findings.body: The provider event listener that disables permissions on RoleRemovedEvent/ClientRemovedEvent/GroupRemovedEvent is now wrapped in `if (Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ))`, checking only the legacy V1 feature. When only ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled (V1 disabled), this block never executes, so no cleanup/disable logic runs at all when a client, role, or group is removed under the V2 fine-grained authorization model. Since the corresponding V2 permission classes (e.g. ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled) throw UnsupportedOperationException, this avoids a crash, but it also means there is no equivalent cleanup path for V2 schema data (e.g. orphaned per-client/per-user resources or policies referencing a removed client, role, or group), risking stale/orphaned authorization data over time.

findings.title: New MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE scope added to Clients schema has no test coverage
findings.body: AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS now includes the MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE scope (used by ClientPermissionsV2.canMapClientScopeRoles), but PermissionClientTest only imports and exercises MAP_ROLES and MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE (see testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient). There is no test validating that granting/denying MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE actually controls the ability to map client-scope roles for a client, leaving this new capability unverified.

findings.title: Several ClientPermissionEvaluator methods unconditionally throw UnsupportedOperationException in V2
findings.body: canExchangeTo, exchangeToPermission, mapRolesPermission, mapRolesClientScopePermission, mapRolesCompositePermission, managePermission, configurePermission, viewPermission, isPermissionsEnabled, setPermissionsEnabled, resource, and getPermissions are all overridden to throw UnsupportedOperationException('Not supported in V2'). If any existing call site (e.g. token exchange flow calling canExchangeTo, or admin console code retrieving a client's permission map via getPermissions/resource) is invoked while ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled, this will propagate as an unchecked RuntimeException resulting in a 500 Internal Server Error instead of a controlled 403/empty response, rather than failing gracefully.
